item.title: Re: How Did You Find the Foundation?
item.content:encoded:
I discovered the foundation in 2017, I think.

I watched a video about the top 10 scariest SCP anomalies, and I remember being scared when I saw SCP-096's face and then the narrator telling me that it will kill me within 2 minutes.

After that I read SCP-049 and SCP-048 on the wiki.

Then I watched youtubers play SCP - Containment Breach and I still remember on how I really wanted to play that game back then because I was ordering a new PC at the time, and the wait was killing me.

And that's how I discovered the site.

item.title: Re: How Did You Find the Foundation?
item.content:encoded:
I ended up finding the foundation on Youtube, after a video of Markiplier playing SPC CB popped up, I found one by the Exploring Series on SCP 3333, the tower. The idea that things like that exist, that they were so… absurd and intriguing drew me in. The mystery and possibility called to me, and then I found the site.

Learning that everything had been written by fans of it amazed me. I love writing and to think that this site has grown on people developing their ideas and working together amazed me. I love the concepts the SCP's have, I love the way the site is maintained… I'm just glad to be here!

item.title: Re: How Did You Find the Foundation?
item.content:encoded: So I was messing around on reddit somewhere, and having a discussion about eldritch horror and bemoaning the lack of good new stuff (this was 2014) other than Caitlin R. Kiernan's books (which I highly recommend) and someone linked me SCP-2480. I read some more of the Sarkic canon, other articles by Meta and then expanded outward. I didn't actually join until 2019, and my exposure has been hit or miss… so I feel like there are well known articles or series that I am still unaware of.

item.title: Re: How Did You Find the Foundation?
item.content:encoded:
+ show block
– hide block

12 year old me loved Five Nights at Freddy's and The Sims 4. I found a youtuber making them in the sims said youtuber also had a creepypasta sims series where she made 173. I also watched another series of hers when she played an rpg made by one of her fans called Creepypasta Town which had the SCP Foundation trying to contain the creepypasta characters except they were called the SCP Force and they had this whole knight theme which I thought was cool so I googled SCP and found the wiki.

There was so much going on and I didn't know what to look at first. then I found the joke SCP's and thought that was a good place to start but there were too many of them so I scrolled to the bottom and found the *sighs* List of Things Dr Bright Is Not Allowed To Do At The Foundation. thought it was hilarious and refused to read anything else. didn't even read 963 until almost 2 years later.

Then in 2017 I actually started reading other things on the wiki but I lost interest until late 2019. I was helping set up for my school's art show when I saw fan art of a bunch of characters like O5-1, Robert Bumaro and Pangloss there were also videos playing of the same person cos plying Bright and Clef. I remembered how much I had liked the wiki and checked out all the stuff I had read before including The List which I now cringe at. I was 15 at that point so I applied for membership a month later and here we are.

item.title: Re: How Did You Find the Foundation?
item.content:encoded: A couple years ago, I found this creepypasta video (forgot the channel, the pasta was called "Trick or Treat" I think") and it had SCP-1471 in the thumbnail. I didn't know what it was at first but thought it looked cool. Anyways fast forward and my friend was watching SCP Illusrated's video on SCP-096 and I asked her about it, she told me it was "shy guy" and I looked it up and got invested. item.title: Re: How Did You Find the Foundation?
item.content:encoded:
I first heard of it through a comedy troupe/YouTube group called LoadingReadyRun; they run their Twitch channel like a TV station, and one of the 'shows' is called Talking Simulator, which looks at game narratives, explores connections to other narratives, art, literature, history, etc. SCP got mentioned various times but I didn't actually look into it at the time.

A few months ago, while putzing around on TV Tropes, I ended up wiki-walking to the Foundation's page, came to the wiki proper through 093, and started reading.

item.title: Re: How Did You Find the Foundation?
item.content:encoded: It was a summer break on 2014 when I was surfing the net. I am a creepypasta reader so it would go without saying that I actually stumbled upon several creepypastas (both bad and well written) about our beloved Peanut (SCP-173). I enjoyed the unique feeling especially how 173 was designed. Not too creepy, not too familiar. It is the perfect blend of bizarreness and terror. I checked the comments on the Wiki and there I discovered that 173 is actually an independent entity from the creepypasta universe. I remember how great it felt when I discovered that he has friends that are equally interesting and so there began my venture as a Foundation "personnel".

item.title: Re: How Did You Find the Foundation?
item.content:encoded:
2017. I discovered the site by the video of a popular French YouTuber, LinksTheSun. I was intrigued, I had read some humorous collaborative pages. It was a good laugh. At the same time, I wanted to have more friends. I made an account.

It's in 2018 that I began to make some English/French translations. After that, at the same time, I became more interested by -EN. I made an application here, had began to talk with people and in the end of the year 2019, I had seen that some Staff teams wanted new JS. CO had accepted my application. And now, I had made many additions to collaborative pages, I'm a critter on forums, an active IRC chatter and I work on my first article for the site.

All of that was totally worth it.

item.title: Re: How Did You Find the Foundation?
item.content:encoded:
It was 2012 and I was really into the slenderman mythos at the time, specifically the Marble Hornets series. I was binging spooky Youtube videos when I came across one that claimed slenderman was real. (At that age I considered he was just as real as sasquatch, which means very real.)

The video claimed the slenderman was actually an "anomaly" and had possibly escaped from the SCP Foundation. The video then went on to explain the Foundation in enough grounded detail to convince me it existed in real life. Sure enough the website was real and it took me a couple weeks to realize it was all fiction. I also discovered the Holders series around then, which is another astounding collaborative horror project. Good times.

I've been a fan ever since. Made a wikidot account back in 2013 but only recently realized I'd never applied to the actual SCP site.

item.title: Re: How Did You Find the Foundation?
item.content:encoded:
Funny story, actually. I was scrolling through Pinterest, minding my own business when I came across a 'Plague Doctor' picture and saved it to one of my boards. More and more of them started popping up and some of the comments mentioned an 'SCP - 049'. At the time, I had no idea what that was, so it was just a jumble of letters and numbers.

Not long after (about a few hours), I searched it, and found it was a popular site with intresting characters. I ended up being roped into it the more my curiosity grew. SCP - 049 has been, and probably always will be, my favorite SCP. (Kudos to the people who made him!). Now, I'm proud to call myself an SCP Member and am excited to get to work on my own SCP. :D

item.title: Re: How Did You Find the Foundation?
item.content:encoded:
I first heard about the Foundation from a comment about SCP-055 on an entirely unrelated website in 2008, back before there were any four-digit SCPs. I actually have a few (very bad) SCPs that still exist in Series I, under a defunct account. Reading the wiki was a very different experience, back then. There was a lot more blood and gore, a lot less character and plot development, and a lot more bumbling researchers causing containment breaches with their wacky antics. There was definitely a lot of charm to the site back then, and plenty of fascinating articles, but it kind of blurred together. It felt like I was reading the same scp over and over, and I drifted away around 2010.

I poked my nose back in around 2017, more or less out of curiosity and nostalgia. I was amazed to find how much the site had grown and flourished in the intervening years. It's less a repository for creepypasta and more a collaborative storytelling website, where hundreds of authors brought different ideas to the table to create something much greater than the sum of its parts. In a lot of ways, I feel like the wiki grew up, and I'm excited to see where it goes next!
